probe: Test whether r259's minimum sink contract can weaken durable full returned-result replay to a durable completion token plus independently verifiable read-after-write without re-opening duplicate external effects under ambiguous timeout, concurrent retry, or idempotency-key expiry.

public_sources.qualification: Expired IETF Internet-Draft; work-in-progress evidence only. It requires resources to publish key-expiration policy, says completed retries SHOULD receive the prior operation result, and concurrent retries SHOULD receive a conflict response.

Internet Standard HTTP Semantics. PUT is defined idempotent for its intended effect; If-None-Match:* can prevent an unsafe method such as PUT from modifying an already-existing target; 202 Accepted is noncommittal and HTTP itself does not provide later asynchronous status delivery.

tested_scope: Documentation-level architectural falsification/derivation only. No external effect, hosted compute, paid/trial API, protected authority, O/downstream/other-worker semantics, manual execution, or quota-bearing service was used. The result applies only where the sink exposes a durable operation/effect identity and independently readable authoritative state. It does not generalize to arbitrary non-addressable side effects.

A_full_result_replay.description: Sink durably stores and replays the full prior response/result for a stable idempotency key.
A_full_result_replay.duplicate_safety: strong when key/payload binding, atomic effect commit, concurrency exclusion, and retention are satisfied

B_completion_token_plus_read_after_write.description: Sink durably binds stable request/effect identity to exactly one operation/effect commit, returns or makes recoverable a stable completion/status token, and permits authoritative read-after-write verification without storing the full response payload.
B_completion_token_plus_read_after_write.duplicate_safety: equivalent to A for the exact effect only if token/key binding is atomic with effect authorization/commit and retries cannot create a second effect
B_completion_token_plus_read_after_write.storage_integration_cost: lower than full response replay when authoritative result state is already addressable
B_completion_token_plus_read_after_write.retry_observability: status/effect resource read rather than cached response replay

C_plain_202_or_token_without_atomic_iden.description: Return 202/token but do not durably and atomically bind it to a unique effect identity.
C_plain_202_or_token_without_atomic_iden.duplicate_safety: fails ambiguous-timeout and concurrent-retry safety; 202 alone is noncommittal

derived_minimum_contract.stable_identity: Client supplies or deterministically derives a stable request/effect identity; payload identity is bound so one key/token cannot authorize divergent effects.
derived_minimum_contract.atomicity: Before or with useful-effect commitment, the sink atomically records the unique identity-to-operation/effect binding such that concurrent retries cannot authorize a second useful effect.
derived_minimum_contract.completion_token: A durable token or deterministic effect/status resource identity survives response loss and identifies the unique operation/effect rather than merely one transport attempt.
derived_minimum_contract.read_after_write: The sink exposes an authoritative read whose observed state is sufficient to distinguish committed/not-committed/failed for the exact useful effect; the client verifies that state after an ambiguous timeout instead of requiring replay of the original response body.
derived_minimum_contract.concurrent_retry: Same-identity concurrent retry is serialized, rejected/conflicted, or resolves to the already-bound operation; it never starts a second useful effect.
derived_minimum_contract.expiry: If idempotency-key/token mapping can expire while a retry is still possible, duplicate safety is lost unless a stronger permanent/deterministic effect identity independently prevents a second commit. Therefore retention must span the maximum retry horizon OR the effect identity itself must remain uniqueness-enforced beyond key expiry.
derived_minimum_contract.result_replay_weakening: Full response/result replay is not itself necessary for duplicate safety when authoritative effect state is independently addressable and the above identity/atomicity/read contract holds. What is necessary is durable unique-effect binding plus recoverable completion evidence.

semantic_conclusion: CONDITIONAL_TRANSVERSAL_WEAKENING_ESTABLISHED: r259's durable returned-result replay requirement can be weakened to durable completion-token/effect-identity replay plus authoritative read-after-write for addressable effects. This preserves exact-effect duplicate safety under response loss and concurrent retry only when unique identity binding is atomic with effect commitment and retained through the retry horizon. Plain 202 Accepted or a token not atomically bound to one useful effect is insufficient. Key expiry before the retry horizon re-opens the duplicate window unless the useful effect itself has a persistent uniqueness/conditional-write identity. Arbitrary sinks and hidden non-idempotent side effects remain unresolved.
conflict_check: Exactly one bounded CLEAN Phase-1 child reconstructed from own r259 state; public specifications only; no other-role/O/downstream/legacy semantics; no scheduler mutation; no wait/poll/backoff/retry; no optional second leaf.
frontier: r258 established internal create-once semantic-effect receipt plus CAS pointer.
r259 established that outbox-only does not close external duplicate delivery and identified atomic sink idempotency as the missing boundary.

r260 weakens full prior-result replay: duplicate safety needs durable unique effect binding and recoverable completion evidence, not necessarily a cached response body, when authoritative effect state is independently readable.
Idempotency mapping expiry is safe only after the retry horizon or when a stronger persistent effect identity independently prevents a second commit.
HTTP method idempotence alone cannot prove hidden application side effects are duplicate-safe; exact useful-effect scope must remain explicit.

Use public specifications only; preserve zero finite-quota/zero-cost constraints; do not start more than one leaf.
